svg.title: Compare observations with a stated inheritance model
svg.desc: The worked parental cross AA×aa gives Aa F1, whose cross gives F2 genotype probabilities one-quarter AA, one-half Aa and one-quarter aa. Four existing synthetic samples are tabulated without completing the learner graph: at n10 the observations are3/5/2 and1/7/2 with expectations2.5/5/2.5; at n100 observations24/51/25 and28/48/24 with expectations25/50/25. Expected count is probability times sample size and need not be an integer. These larger samples are closer overall but do not establish a guarantee that every category improves as sample size grows. Repeatability, scoring and survival matter. Reciprocal crosses exchange parental-sex contributions. The table is a teaching reference, not empirical Mendel data.

g.text: Compare observations with a stated inheritance model
Exact synthetic counts from the teaching example; observations and expectations stay separate.
P: AA × aa → F1: all Aa → F1 cross: Aa × Aa
F2 model: ¼ AA, ½ Aa, ¼ aa. Score the trait before grouping phenotypes.
Expected count = model probability × sample size; an expectation may be fractional.
Repeat crosses, retain actual counts and check scoring/survival; exact ratios are not required.
Reciprocal crosses exchange which parental sex contributes each phenotype.
